:::{#sol-orthogonal-complement-subspace-practice}

A vector $\vecf{u}$ is in $\mathcal{X}^\perp$ exactly when
$(1, 0, 1) \cdot \vecf{u} = u_1 + u_3 = 0$
and $(1, 0, -1) \cdot \vecf{u} = u_1 - u_3 = 0$.
Adding the two equations gives $u_1 = 0$,
and then $u_3 = 0$,
while $u_2$ is free.
So

$$
\mathcal{X}^\perp = \cb{(0, u_2, 0) : u_2 \in \reals} = \operatorname{span}\cb{(0, 1, 0)},
$$

the second coordinate axis,
which is a [subspace](linear-algebra-subspaces.qmd#def-subspace),
as @thm-orthogonal-complement-subspace says.

:::
